header: What duty managers see on Tuesday morning
lead: One screen shows the whole week. These are the five parts a duty manager uses most.
caption: The week planner, Wednesday of a spring week at a three-till branch.

callouts.title: The day columns
callouts.text: Seven days across, staff down the side. Drag a shift anywhere and the checks run before you drop it.

callouts.title: The rule strip
callouts.text: A red edge on a shift means a rule would be broken. Hover over it to see the rule in plain words, not a code.

callouts.title: The budget line
callouts.text: Wage cost for the week so far against the branch target, updating as you plan.

callouts.title: The unfilled tray
callouts.text: Shifts with nobody assigned yet. The goal is to empty it by Friday.

callouts.title: The publish button
callouts.text: Greyed out until the week meets every rule. One press sends it to every phone.

image.alternative: Printed shift schedules pinned to a noticeboard in a staff corridor.
